newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia creates A$1 bln fund for 100th birthday.
newsitem.headline: Australia creates A$1 bln fund for 100th birthday.

text.p: The Australian government on Tuesday established a special A$1 billion fund to celebrate the centenary of the country's federation in 1901.
Treasurer Peter Costello, announcing the budget for the fiscal year from July, said the money would pay for projects of national significance, including infrastructure.
"Naturally, it will be a time for remembering and marking our achievements," Costello told Parliament.

The fund was one of the major new announcements in a cautious budget that achieves an underlying deficit -- excluding one-offs such as asset sales -- of A$3.853 billion, compared with a deficit of A$6.856 billion in 1996/97.
Costello said A$600 million would be spent between 1998/99 and 2000/01 and the rest after that, mostly in the next year.

Projects will be selected in consultation with states and territories and will include a long-planned national museum in Canberra and an institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander studies, also in Canberra.

Unlike the A$1.25 billion conservation fund which is paid for from the proceeds of the partial sale of telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp, the Federation Fund will be funded by savings in government spending, the budget papers show.
Australia was formed by the federation of British colonies in 1901.
